diagnostic_features.evidence: Pycnidia are found in the necrotic tissue and tarda refers to the late appearance of septa in conidia and the slow maturing habit of pycnospores (Stewart, 1957). The pycnidia are 70-110 microns in diameter.

type_of_disease.evidence: The phoma stain, Phoma spp., is a fungal disease that occurs in several countries around the world where coffee is grown in areas of higher altitudes.

affected_parts.evidence: the fungus attacks leaves, flowers, fruits and branches of the coffee plant, producing very characteristic lesions

summary.value: On leaves, the disease produces circular dark spots of varying sizes (up to 2 cm in diameter); on affected branches, dark depressed lesions appear that can involve the entire diameter (dry shoots); it can also cause necrosis of flowers and fruits in floral rosettes.
summary.evidence: On the leaves of the second and subsequent pairs of leaves, the disease produces circular spots of dark color and varying sizes, which can reach 2 cm in diameter (Fig. 2). In the affected branches, a symptom also called dry shoots (Fig. 3), dark depressed lesions are seen, which can involve the entire diameter.

diagnostic_features.value: Infection begins at the apical part in terminal shoots and tender leaves; when lesions reach leaf edges, leaves curve and may present cracks; circular dark spots up to 2 cm on older leaves; dark depressed lesions on branches that can involve the entire diameter (dry shoots); necrosis of flowers and fruits in floral rosettes.
diagnostic_features.evidence: the infection begins at the apical part, in the terminal shoot, in the tender leaves, which still have no physical barriers of resistance, reaching the young tissues. When the lesions reach the edges of the leaves, they curve, may present cracks

look_alikes.evidence: the symptom can easily be confused with boron deficiency (Fig. 1)

diagnostic_features.value: Suprastomatal, bouquet-shaped, orange-coloured uredinia (orange pustules) protruding through the stomata on the lower leaf surface approximately 3 weeks after infection; chlorotic spots as the first macroscopic symptom; premature leaf fall/severe defoliation.
diagnostic_features.evidence: Approximately 3 weeks after infection, urediniosporic sori protrude through the stomata in a bouquet shape. These appear as orange‐coloured pustules, the typical sign of this disease

value: Hemileia coffeicola (produces sori scattered throughout the leaf and presents urediniospores with fewer but larger spines)
